query: What visit-note signals suggest a longer visit?

per_column.name: num_conditions
per_column.rationale: Count of documented conditions is a clinical complexity signal derived from the note that plausibly drives longer visits without restating or leaking duration.

per_column.name: has_procedure
per_column.rationale: Whether a procedure occurred is a legitimate visit characteristic that plausibly increases time; not a function of duration itself.

per_column.name: has_multiple_meds
per_column.rationale: Polypharmacy flag reflects patient complexity and reconciliation effort, a plausible predictor outside the focus. Very imbalanced (7/250) so weak signal, but still valid.

per_column.name: note_length
per_column.rationale: Note length is a borderline generic surface feature, but longer notes plausibly correlate with more involved visits and it is not a deterministic function of duration; treated as a weak predictor.

per_column.name: is_urgent_note
per_column.rationale: Urgency signal extracted from the note is a plausible driver of visit length and lies outside the focus variable; partially redundant with existing 'urgency' column but still predictive.

per_column.name: has_diagnostics
per_column.rationale: Presence of diagnostic tests is a visit activity that plausibly extends duration; a legitimate predictor, not a restatement or post-outcome leak.

judge.rationale: All six added columns are legitimate note-derived predictors that lie outside visit_duration_min without restating or leaking it. The complexity/activity flags (num_conditions, has_procedure, has_diagnostics) carry the strongest and most balanced signal; is_urgent_note overlaps with the existing urgency column, note_length is a weak generic surface feature, and has_multiple_meds is heavily imbalanced. As a set they give solid but not exceptional incremental leverage.
